messages:
dmitri: Quick q — as we onboard more sparse/sharded safetensors models the warmup phase is suddenly our biggest IO spike on startup. wondering if we should formalize a QoS / two-phase warmup rather than the current all-or-nothing prefetch.

katie: I think two-phase is the right call. Phase 1 = cheap index/probe to build a hot-row map. Phase 2 = prioritized prefetch of hot rows/kv. Map QoS lanes to per-request priority header (e.g. X-Weight-Priority) so router can tag warmup traffic.

ben: +1. For sparse layers we can avoid loading entire matrices — load by row popularity. We should define priority buckets: critical (attention kv), high (lm_head), normal (ffn).

alice: Also add a startup token-budget so a model doesn't warm up millions of tokens at once. Soft-warm vs hard-warm: soft warms in background and serves fallback cold reads. Hard-warm blocks until token_budget satisfied. Default = soft.

carla: caveat: on NFS/remote filesystems high parallel prefetch kills metadata server. We need adaptive concurrency and IOPS-aware backoff. Something like: if iops_util > 70% lower parallelism and increase probe size.

katie: propose a minimal config prototype (sketch):
```
warmup:
  probe_phase:
    probe_bytes: 65536  # read small prefixes to estimate hot rows
    max_parallel_reads: 8
  prefetch_phase:
    token_budget: 20000
    qos_class: background
    hot_rows_only: true
    concurrency_backoff: true
```

dmitri: nice. Implementation notes: 1) probe phase should be `read(0, probe_bytes)` across shards to build a lightweight frequency estimate, 2) maintain per-model hot-row LRU tracked in serving runtime, 3) expose a warmup-scoped trace id so we can correlate heavy reads.

ben: implementation idea: expose a `warmup_priority` on the weightsource API so callers can supply: {priority, token_budget, allow_blocking}. Runtime will enqueue warmup tasks into priority queues and use `aiofiles`-style read with semaphore for concurrency.

carla: plus set a per-file descriptor rate limiter when underlying FS is remote. For local SSD it's fine to be more aggressive. We should detect device type at mount-time and tune defaults.

eva: metrics we need: warmup_bytes_read, warmup_duration_seconds, warmup_stalled_reads, warmup_token_budget_used, warmup_io_wait_percent. These should appear in Console per-model and per-route so product can see cost impact.

ben: I'll add a Prom counter + histogram for bytes/read latency. Will open a PR to add `warmup_priority` to WeightSource API.

dmitri: for rollout plan — start as opt-in flag on Dedicated and Private, then enable for hosted for low-risk tiers. Need a canary where prefetchs are off and we collect metrics first.

deploy-bot: Ticket #5012 created: "sparse warmup QoS and adaptive prefetch" assigned to ben.

katie: :thumbsup:
